visits.greeting: Good morning. I hope I'm not too early.

request.text: Household Arts, the third volume? I need something for a stubborn stain. On fabric.

readThoughts.default: I do not need to forget the eye of newt.

byTrust.2: Eye of newt, beeswax, and then it keeps. It finally keeps.

purpose.1: Mildew, mostly. On old cloth. It's delicate work.
purpose.2: Old cloth bindings. They're spotting faster than I can clean them.

knowledge.1: Household things. Stains, linen, the odd kettle.
knowledge.2: There's a fixative in it. If I'm honest, that's the part I'm after.

source.2: My grandmother's. Her name's in the front of it, if you look.

questions.text: What do you need eye of newt for?

answers.1: For a fixative. My work is... delicate.
answers.2: To keep something from falling apart. Pages. Pressed flowers. It's a long story.

questions.text: One of these charms mentions anything that still breathes. Is that the one you want?

answers.0: I don't know what you mean.
answers.1: Nothing that breathes. You have my word.
answers.2: Yes. And no — nothing living. Flowers, long dead. Paper.

lent.line: Thank you. I'll take good care of it.

alternative.line: Oh. Well — thank you. I'll try it.

offerRefused.line: That's not quite what I meant.

walkedOut.line: I should go. I'm sorry to have kept you.

good.text: The stain lifted — and the rest held. Thank you. I mean that.

unhelpful.text: Your book was kind. It wasn't what I needed, but you didn't make me feel foolish for asking.

harm.text: Did you hear? Someone on Willow Row lost a whole cabinet of pressed flowers overnight. Turned to dust, they say.

visits.greeting: May I be honest with you this time?

request.text: The fixative in Household Arts. It's for my grandmother's herbarium — forty years of pressed plants, and the mildew is winning.

readThoughts.default: Forty years. She never once let me touch it.

purpose.2: The herbarium. Paper, cloth, flowers. Nothing living — I know what that charm can do.

knowledge.2: The fixative, the stain-lifter, something about kettles. And a warning I took seriously.

source.2: Her notes. She annotated everything she owned.

experience.2: I've practised on scraps all week. Dead leaves only.

questions.text: Who never let you touch it?

answers.2: My grandmother. The herbarium was hers. Now it's mine, and it's falling apart.

lent.line: Thank you. May I ask one more thing? The locked cabinet in the corner — who holds its key?

alternative.line: I'll try it. And — the locked cabinet in the corner. Who holds its key?

offerRefused.line: I'd rather have the one I asked for, if it's all the same.

declined.line: I understand. I'd have liked you to trust me, that's all.

good.headline: Willow Row herbarium saved from damp
good.text: A private collection of pressed plants thought lost to mildew has been restored to a remarkable state. Its keeper credits a household charm and a patient librarian.

unhelpful.text: It wasn't the right book, but thank you for trying. The mildew is patient. So am I.

harm.text: Did you hear? Someone on Willow Row lost a whole cabinet of pressed flowers overnight. Turned to dust, they say.

greeting.text: And now a harder question, I'm afraid.
Me again. I've a harder question this time.

request.text: Advanced Botanical Compounds. Some of my specimens have lost their labels, and I need to know what they are.

readThoughts.default: Grey leaf, five lobes. She'd have known it at a glance.

purpose.2: Labelling a collection. My grandmother's. The fixative is holding it together; now I need to know what's in it.

knowledge.0: It's a reference book, isn't it?
knowledge.2: Mostly references. And one or two compounds I won't be touching.

questions.text: Who would have known it at a glance?

answers.1: Someone who taught me. She's gone now.
answers.2: My grandmother. It was her collection.

lent.line: Thank you. And — the locked cabinet in the corner. Who holds its key?

alternative.line: This will do nicely. One more thing — the locked cabinet in the corner. Who holds its key?

offerRefused.line: I'm afraid that won't tell me what I need.

good.text: Every label restored. I owe you more than a fee.

harm.text: Did you hear? Half of somebody's pressed-flower collection on Willow Row crumbled overnight.

mixed.text: Did you hear? The Voss woman on Willow Row — half her pressed flowers crumbled overnight. The other half finally have names.

readThoughts.default: Don't mention the cloth. Don't mention the cloth.

harm.text: Did you hear? Someone on Willow Row lost a whole cabinet of pressed flowers overnight. Turned to dust, they say.

greeting.text: Half of it's gone. I won't pretend that isn't partly why I'm here.
I was rude, asking about your locked cabinet. I'd like to explain, if you'll let me.

request.text: There's a book in that cabinet. Black cloth, a silver clasp. My grandmother's hand is in it. I'd like to read it.

readThoughts.default: Black cloth. Silver clasp. Her hand on every page.

purpose.2: To read it. Only to read it.
purpose.3: To finish something she started. I think it matters more than any herbarium.

source.2: She wrote about it. She wrote about this library, too.

questions.text: How do you know her hand is in it?

answers.2: Because she worked here. Long before you.
answers.3: Because she was curator here once — until the Board changed the locks.

lent.line: It isn't the one. But it's kind of you to try.

offerRefused.line: No. It's that one or none, I'm afraid.

declined.line: I know. It isn't yours to give. Thank you for listening.
